intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that orofaciodigital syndrome XVIII (OFD18) is caused by homozygous mutation in the IFT57 gene on chromosome 3q13.

checks.claim: Orofaciodigital syndrome XVIII (OFD18) is caused by homozygous mutation in the IFT57 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: we report on a unique consanguineous family with an unclassified type of OFDS with short stature and brachymesophalangia overlapping with EVCS, and caused by a homozygous hypomorphic mutation of IFT57
checks.explanation: The paper describes the disorder as an unclassified OFDS. 'OFD18' is OMIM's name for it.

checks.claim: The IFT57 gene is located on chromosome 3q13.
checks.evidence_quote: an IFT57 synonymous variation (chr3:g.107910368C>T, c.777G>A, p.Lys259Lys, RefSeq accession number NM_018010.3)
checks.explanation: The paper places the variant on chromosome 3. The 3q13 band is standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Orofaciodigital syndrome XVIII is an autosomal recessive ciliopathy. Like the other forms of orofaciodigital syndrome, it is defined by abnormalities of the oral cavity, face, and digits, including features such as oral frenulae, cleft lip and/or palate, and polydactyly.

checks.claim: Orofaciodigital syndrome XVIII is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Autosomal recessive IFT57 hypomorphic mutation cause ciliary transport defect in unclassified oral-facial-digital syndrome
checks.explanation: The title states autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: Orofaciodigital syndrome XVIII is a ciliopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: highlights the first description of a ciliary transport defect in OFDS, extending the genetic heterogeneity of this subgroup of ciliopathies.
checks.explanation: The paper calls OFDS a subgroup of ciliopathies and reports a ciliary transport defect in this form.

checks.claim: Orofaciodigital syndromes are defined by abnormalities of the oral cavity, face, and digits.
checks.evidence_quote: The Oral-Facial-Digital syndromes (OFDS) are a heterogeneous group of disorders having common oral, facial, and digital malformations.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the syndromes as sharing oral, facial and digital malformations.

checks.claim: Orofaciodigital syndromes can include oral frenulae.
checks.evidence_quote: oral anomalies such as tongue hamartomas, oral frenulae, cleft palate, abnormal teething
checks.explanation: Oral frenulae are listed among the oral anomalies.

checks.claim: Orofaciodigital syndromes can include cleft lip and/or palate.
checks.evidence_quote: oral anomalies such as tongue hamartomas, oral frenulae, cleft palate, abnormal teething; ii) facial dysmorphism such as hypertelorism, lateral or medial cleft lip
checks.explanation: Both cleft palate and cleft lip are listed.

checks.evidence_quote: digital anomalies such as pre-, meso- or post-axial polydactyly, abnormal Y-shaped metacarpes, or syndactylies
checks.explanation: Polydactyly is listed among the digital anomalies.

paragraphs.text: OFD18 is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern, as shown by the homozygous IFT57 mutation found in the reported consanguineous family (Thevenon et al., 2016).

checks.claim: OFD18 is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: Autosomal recessive IFT57 hypomorphic mutation cause ciliary transport defect in unclassified oral-facial-digital syndrome
checks.explanation: The title states autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: A homozygous IFT57 mutation was found in the reported OFD18 family.
checks.evidence_quote: Sanger sequencing confirmed the variation at a homozygous status in the 3 affected subjects.
checks.explanation: The mutation was homozygous in all three affected siblings.

checks.claim: The reported OFD18 family with the IFT57 mutation was consanguineous.
checks.evidence_quote: A unique consanguineous family presenting with an unclassified OFDS with skeletal dysplasia and brachymesophalangia was explored.
checks.explanation: The paper describes the family as consanguineous.

paragraphs.text: Orofaciodigital syndromes are a genetically heterogeneous group of disorders. Most of the known causal genes encode proteins that act at the primary cilium or the centrosome.

checks.claim: Orofaciodigital syndromes are a genetically heterogeneous group of disorders.
checks.evidence_quote: Thus, an unclassified type of OFDS was evoked, once more underlying the clinical and genetic heterogeneity of OFDS.
checks.explanation: The paper states that OFDS is genetically heterogeneous.

checks.claim: Most of the known genes that cause orofaciodigital syndromes encode proteins that act at the primary cilium or the centrosome.
checks.evidence_quote: While most OFDS are ciliopathies caused by mutated centrosomal proteins (OFD1, SCLT1 and TBC1D32/C6orf170) or components of the transition zone (TMEM216 and TCNT3).
checks.explanation: Most known causal genes encode centrosomal proteins or ciliary transition-zone components.

paragraphs.text: Thevenon et al. (2016) performed whole-exome sequencing in a consanguineous family with an orofaciodigital syndrome phenotype. They found a homozygous mutation in the IFT57 gene, which encodes a component of the intraflagellar transport complex B. This tied the disorder to defective ciliary intraflagellar transport.

checks.claim: Thevenon et al. (2016) performed whole-exome sequencing in a consanguineous family with an orofaciodigital syndrome phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity mapping and exome sequencing led to the identification of a homozygous mutation in IFT57
checks.explanation: Exome sequencing was done in an affected member of the consanguineous OFDS family.

checks.claim: Thevenon et al. (2016) found a homozygous mutation in the IFT57 gene in a consanguineous family with orofaciodigital syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity mapping and exome sequencing led to the identification of a homozygous mutation in IFT57, which encodes a protein implicated in ciliary transport.
checks.explanation: The paper reports this finding directly.

checks.claim: The IFT57 gene encodes a component of intraflagellar transport complex B.
checks.evidence_quote: However, further analysis indicated that IFT57 is a subunit of intraflagellar transport complex B.

checks.claim: The finding of a homozygous IFT57 mutation tied orofaciodigital syndrome XVIII to defective ciliary intraflagellar transport.
checks.evidence_quote: This report identifies the implication of IFT57 in human pathology and highlights the first description of a ciliary transport defect in OFDS
checks.explanation: The paper links the IFT57 mutation to defective ciliary (anterograde intraflagellar) transport in OFDS.

references.label: Thevenon et al. (2016)
